response.sql: SELECT AVG(UnitPrice) AS avg_unit_price, AVG(Bytes * 1.0 / Milliseconds) AS avg_bytes_per_ms FROM Track WHERE Bytes > 10323804 AND Milliseconds > 0;

assumptions.assumption: A large track has Bytes strictly greater than 10323804. NULL Bytes is excluded by the comparison, and Milliseconds > 0 guards against division by zero.

The average bytes per millisecond is the mean of each track's own Bytes/Milliseconds ratio, computed as a real division (Bytes * 1.0) so the result is not truncated to an integer. AVG ignores any NULL ratios.

alternatives.interpretation: Bytes per millisecond is the overall ratio of total bytes to total milliseconds across the large tracks, rather than the mean of per-track ratios.
alternatives.sql: SELECT AVG(UnitPrice) AS avg_unit_price, SUM(Bytes) * 1.0 / SUM(Milliseconds) AS avg_bytes_per_ms FROM Track WHERE Bytes > 10323804 AND Milliseconds > 0;
